name: Ramp
text: Add a visible server-side skip link at the top of every page. It’s the only reliable way to let keyboard users bypass repetitive navigation blocks instantly. The trade-off is a small extra server hit for every page load, but that’s trivial compared to the barrier it removes for people who rely on keyboards.

name: Reader
text: A visible server-side skip link may disrupt the visual flow of the page for some users. Instead, consider using a combination of ARIA landmarks and an invisible skip link that only appears when focused. This will maintain usability while avoiding visual clutter and respecting design aesthetics. To settle the argument, user testing with diverse groups could reveal the better approach for accessibility without sacrificing design integrity.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a client-side skip link that appears only when keyboard focus reaches the first interactive element. This keeps the page clean for mouse users while guaranteeing keyboard users can bypass blocks instantly—no server load, no visual disruption. The trade-off is a tiny JavaScript dependency, but it’s worth it to avoid forcing every page load to include a skip link that most users never need.

name: Reader
text: The client-side skip link still fails when JavaScript is disabled or slow to load—keyboard users get trapped. A hybrid approach works best: server-render the skip link but hide it by default, then reveal it only on focus via CSS. That removes visual clutter, keeps keyboard access reliable, and needs no JavaScript. Ship it and test with a screen reader.
